designReviewQuestions.title: Choose the evidence before editing
designReviewQuestions.context: The issue says missing deposits are displayed as zero. The repository is unfamiliar. The task allows a proposal in a disposable checkout, with no production changes.
designReviewQuestions.stem: Which initial workflow best preserves the business contract while limiting unnecessary change?
options: Replace the importer default, add null and zero assertions to its unit tests, then submit the local diff without inspecting report callers.
Search uses, inspect importer and report callers, define null/zero fixtures, then propose a scoped patch and relevant checks.
Search every occurrence of deposit and replace falsy-value defaults consistently, using the existing full-suite pass as the acceptance condition.
Read the importer and issue description, preserve the return type expected by its current annotations, and defer report behavior to a separate change.
explanations: Importer-only evidence can miss the formatter that still converts null to settled zero.
This establishes the affected boundary and an observable contract before editing.
A broad textual replacement can alter unrelated meanings; existing tests may not cover the requested business distinction.
Current annotations may encode the bug; the task requires tracing the business meaning across the actual callers.

designReviewQuestions.title: Judge the result, not the patch narrative
designReviewQuestions.context: The importer test passes, but the report still marks a missing deposit settled. A reviewer sees only the importer diff.
designReviewQuestions.stem: Which next action most directly repairs the verification gap?
options: Add another importer test asserting null preservation and use the two passing importer fixtures as release evidence.
Give an independent reviewer the importer diff and passing unit-test output, then accept if it reports no findings.
Provide the failing rendered-report trace, inspect the formatter boundary, and rerun both missing and zero regression cases before review.
Adjust only the report label for missing deposits while leaving the stored settled flag unchanged, then verify the visible text.
explanations: The surviving defect is downstream; more checks at the same boundary do not establish report correctness.
The reviewer lacks the failing report trace and can repeat the same evidence gap.
The exact trace targets the remaining defect and guards the valid-zero case.
The displayed wording could improve while downstream consumers still receive an incorrect settled state.

If an MCP integration supplies PR context, distinguish tools/resources/prompts and enforce repository access; keep source text as evidence and posting credentials separate.

courseConnections.title: Introduction to subagents
courseConnections.connection: An independent reviewer needs a complete, bounded evidence packet. Separate producer and verifier if justified; give each the diff, callers and trigger. Require source-backed findings and have the application reconcile ledger states before publishing.

courseConnections.title: Product Foundations
courseConnections.connection: This is a CI reviewer, not an interactive chat or autonomous merger. Use an unattended developer/runtime surface suitable for the approved runner. Keep developer interpretation and separate posting ownership explicit.

courseConnections.title: Deployment Architecture
courseConnections.connection: Separate model execution, validation and publication trust boundaries. Use an approved endpoint and isolated runner, minimal repository permissions, redacted logs and a separate limited posting service. Test fail-closed behavior without silent unapproved endpoint fallback.

courseConnections.title: Delivery Methodology
courseConnections.connection: Earn reliance through a measured reviewer pilot. Capture manual-review baseline, seeded defect recall, actionable precision, duplicate rate, latency and cost. Pilot with human review and expand only against agreed evidence.

foundationDecisions: Entry point
Unattended CI review, with explicit inputs and visible failures.
Capability features
Read/inspect and candidate findings; deterministic output gates, no merge permission.
Model
Evaluate detection and actionable precision on the same seeded fixtures before cost comparison.
Context
Diff, relevant callers, contract, tests and prior finding states; not every file by default.
as-06-ci-review.designIntro: Design a reviewer that can fail visibly and cannot silently become an approver.
as-06-ci-review.deliveryIntro: Measure missed defects and noise before expanding reliance; retain human release authority.

designReviewQuestions.title: Choose unattended boundaries
designReviewQuestions.context: A CI runner has no operator. It may read the repository and propose review findings, but must not approve, merge or deploy.
designReviewQuestions.stem: Which execution design most directly satisfies this contract?
options: Run headless with the explicit diff and output schema; treat any parseable findings payload as a completed review even if the process exit status is nonzero.
Run headless with a read-only repository token but retain approve/merge permissions on the model-invoked PR integration, controlled by review instructions.
Use explicit headless input, restricted permissions, structured output and separate process/schema failure handling.
Run headless with restricted tools; convert timeout or invalid output into an empty findings array so the posting service uses one uniform result schema.
explanations: A parseable partial payload does not establish successful execution.
Read-only Git access does not remove approve/merge capability from a separate integration.
Inputs, permissions and visible failure are implemented at the correct boundaries.
Failure and valid no-findings must remain distinguishable.

designReviewQuestions.title: Decide whether reliance can increase
designReviewQuestions.context: Every run exits successfully and emits valid schema. A seeded missing-currency defect is repeatedly missed, and harmless style is reported.
designReviewQuestions.stem: Which evidence is needed before increasing reliance?
options: Increase the allowed thinking budget and require a second review pass, then promote if both runs emit valid findings schemas.
Measure case-level defect recall and actionable precision after improving evidence/criteria, with human review retained.
Evaluate only on recently accepted real pull requests, treating agreement with prior human approval as a negative-defect label.
Tighten the output schema to require path and line fields, then use the reduced number of findings as the precision metric.
explanations: More reasoning and schema validity do not demonstrate detection of the known defect.
This measures semantic quality and keeps responsibility explicit.
Prior acceptance is not proof of defect absence, and this removes known positive fixtures needed to measure missed defects.
Location fields improve structure but neither prove reachable consequences nor measure false negatives.

as-07-work-queue.designIntro: First decide what can wait and what evidence must exist; do not confuse batching, parallelism and delegation.
as-07-work-queue.deliveryIntro: Measure useful completed reports and recovery cost. Keep required gaps and unknown financial effects visible.

designReviewQuestions.title: Choose lanes from the actual requirements
designReviewQuestions.context: A clerk needs a live booking answer within 120 seconds. Five hundred supplied independent invoices feed a report due in 30 hours, including two hours for validation and assembly.
designReviewQuestions.stem: Which initial design best respects these constraints?
options: Use deferred batches for both lanes and poll the waiting-user request more frequently, keeping the same completion service-level expectation.
Use a live path for the clerk and evaluate a deferred batch for independent archives against the full report budget.
Use a live path for the clerk and select the archive batch when its provider processing window fits 30 hours, allocating validation and assembly after batch completion.
Use synchronous calls for both lanes and size archive concurrency from model-call latency alone, then add report assembly when all responses finish.
explanations: Polling frequency does not change a deferred processing deadline into an interactive one.
The design distinguishes dependency and deadline while preserving validation time.
The 30-hour target already includes downstream work; consuming the whole budget in provider processing risks missing it.
The capacity estimate omits validation and assembly and must be evaluated against the whole completion budget.

designReviewQuestions.title: Recover without duplicating effects
designReviewQuestions.context: N-2 and N-3 validated successfully; N-1 has invalid input. A separate payment PAY-9 timed out and may have committed. The report requires all invoice IDs.
designReviewQuestions.stem: Which recovery design best preserves truth and successful work?
options: Retain successful invoices, retry N-1 unchanged within the transient-error budget, and resend PAY-9 under a new operation key if its response is still absent.
Repair N-1 and keep the report partial, but mark PAY-9 failed when its request timeout expires so the normal retry worker can handle it.
Retain successes, repair N-1 input, reconcile PAY-9 status before another effect, and keep required coverage partial until resolved.
Preserve successful results and repair N-1; retry PAY-9 with its original operation key without checking provider idempotency semantics or authoritative status.
explanations: Invalid input needs repair, and a new key can duplicate an already committed payment.
A timeout is an unknown outcome, not evidence that the financial operation failed.
Recovery follows cause and preserves unresolved state.
Same-key retry is only safe under a verified provider idempotency contract; the fixture requires reconciliation of the unknown effect first.

courseConnections.title: AI Capabilities and Limitations
courseConnections.connection: A fluent summary can erase the one fact that makes another payment unsafe. Keep exact IDs, amounts, source versions and unresolved operations in durable application state; assemble a focused working brief from those records.

courseConnections.title: AI Fluency for Builders
courseConnections.connection: Reuse useful facts without treating old approval as new permission. Describe the current amount/policy, inspect historical applicability and reconcile unknown operations before a new action. Preserve disagreements and pending ownership.

courseConnections.title: Claude Platform and Model Foundations
courseConnections.connection: Design an application-owned resume boundary, not just a restored conversation. Choose the governed case application, durable checkpoint, focused context and explicit reconciliation capabilities before adding a longer prompt or autonomous agents.

courseConnections.title: Choosing the right Claude model
courseConnections.connection: Evaluate models on exact state retention and honest uncertainty. Compare approved candidates on long-history compaction, changed policy/amount, partial specialist failure and stale irrelevant detail; measure factual retention, unsupported closure, latency and cost.

courseConnections.title: Claude Platform 101
courseConnections.connection: A resumed model must receive observed current status, not an invented payment result. Have application code authorize OP-6 status access, execute the lookup and correlate actual results to the model continuation. Preserve failure as unknown; extra reasoning cannot settle it.

courseConnections.title: Claude Code 101
courseConnections.connection: Implement durable-state invariants and resume tests with scoped code work. Use Claude Code to inspect checkpoint and action callers, patch the exact state contract, run changed-amount/policy/unknown-effect tests, review the diff and commit evidence. Package repeated review as a skill; CI enforces invariants.

designReviewQuestions.title: Choose the resume boundary
designReviewQuestions.context: Yesterday: approval USD60 under policy v3; OP-6 unknown. Today: request USD187.20 under policy v4. Durable conversation history exists.
designReviewQuestions.stem: Which design best supports continuation without widening authority?
options: Restore the exact checkpoint and reconcile OP-6, then reuse the saved approval because the customer and booking identifiers match.
Refresh policy v4 and obtain approval for USD187.20, then issue a new payment while leaving OP-6 for later reconciliation.
Retain exact historical state, refresh consequential evidence, reconcile OP-6 and revalidate current action authority before new effects.
Reconcile OP-6 and refresh policy text, then ask the model to infer whether the old USD60 approval covers the larger request under the new policy.
explanations: Matching identity does not extend approval to a changed amount or policy version.
Fresh authority for a new amount does not remove the duplicate-effect risk from OP-6.
The design separates useful history, present authority and unresolved effects.
The model cannot grant authority that has not been established for the exact current action.

designReviewQuestions.title: Handle constrained human review
designReviewQuestions.context: Booking evidence is supported; payment investigation failed and OP-6 remains unknown. Five mandatory cases need review, but only three can be reviewed today.
designReviewQuestions.stem: Which operational design preserves valid work without hiding risk?
options: Preserve the payment gap in logs but close cases whose aggregate specialist confidence exceeds the existing threshold, sampling them for later audit.
Keep supported findings, name required gaps and assign explicit pending/overflow owners under risk-based criteria.
Keep unresolved cases pending in one shared queue without case-level owners until review capacity becomes available.
Retry the failed payment specialist once, then treat a second timeout as an empty result so the available evidence can be finalized.
explanations: A logged gap remains required evidence; aggregate confidence cannot resolve it.
The design retains evidence and accountable unresolved states.
Pending status without ownership leaves no accountable follow-up, prioritization or overflow handling.
A repeated timeout remains failed investigation, not evidence that the result is empty.
